result.title: What the Loss Curve Misses: FP4 Pretraining Slows the Acquisition of Rare Facts
result.summary: Low-precision pretraining is usually judged by validation loss. We ask whether matching loss also means learning rare facts as efficiently. We train transformers from scratch with emulated 4-bit matrix multiplications on synthetic biographies with controlled exposure counts, on their own and mixed into web text. NVFP4 needs 1.32$\times$ and 1.52$\times$ as many exposures as BF16 to match its recall while validation loss differs by only 0.5% and 2%, and 1.26$\times$ and 1.30$\times$ when both models are evaluated with BF16 matrix multiplications. Under our primary readout, the exposure cost is about 1.2$\times$ at matched loss. Zero-mean gradient noise reproduces the cost of quantizing only the backward pass, which barely moves the loss. In a controlled experiment at twice the NVFP4 error, noise fed only to Adam's second-moment estimate acts like a lower learning rate and its cost fades, whereas noise in the update lowers its signal-to-noise ratio and carries about two thirds of the cost through the end of training. Raising the learning rate to offset the smaller average step does not recover the cost, either for this noise or for NVFP4. Gradient statistics of BF16 checkpoints rank the costs of formats, partial quantizations and noise controls without fitting (Spearman 0.96). We suggest measuring rare-fact acquisition alongside loss when evaluating low-precision recipes.

AI.brief_summary: 论文用合成传记在受控曝光次数下从头训练 transformer，比较 NVFP4 与 BF16 在验证损失几乎持平时召回稀有事实所需曝光次数的差距，并定位到梯度噪声、Adam 二阶矩与更新中的噪声的成本来源。
AI.relevance_reason: 「损失曲线掩盖稀有事实获取效率」与 LVR 关注的内部状态是否保留任务必要细节、信息坍缩相近，其按梯度统计预测信息损失成本的思路可供核查是否能用于诊断视觉细节在 latent 中的保留程度。
